_comment: THE AXIS CONTRACT — single source of truth for what each level means. Frozen in unificacion.txt section 12.B; if a rules file contradicts this, the rules file is wrong. The level answers ONE question: how much of the work is the user's? Everything else (how much the agent explains, which rungs it may use, what it hands off) is a consequence, not a second dial.
_axis_comment: The pedagogical axis is 1-5, monotonic: higher = more of the work is yours. 6 is NOT the continuation of that line — it is the axis switched OFF (see off_ramp). Treating it as level 6 of the same scale would make every consumer that assumes monotonicity (calibration, autonomy report, budget) wrong in silence.
_budget_comment: Two knobs, deliberately separated — they were conflated in the v0.4 scaffold window and that is why its numbers were backwards. files_per_day is relief from TEDIUM, and tedium does not scale with level (typing package.json costs the same at L1 and L5), so it stays roughly flat and small. statements_per_file is how much of the THINKING is still the agent's, and that is exactly what the level is for, so that one scales. max_lines_per_new_file is flat for the same reason as files_per_day. null = unlimited.
_shape_comment: Layer 1 of the RU-3 mitigation. The gate cannot detect 'this is an implementation' — that is an open semantic problem and the model can always out-invent a blacklist. So it asserts the opposite, closed property: 'this HAS THE SHAPE OF A SKELETON'. Every line is classified into exactly one category and STATEMENT is the RESIDUAL one, so unknown syntax, an unlisted language, or any trick nobody anticipated all count as implementation and consume budget. The check FAILS CLOSED by construction rather than by enumeration.
_polarity_warning: This detector is deliberately RESTRICTIVE ('when in doubt, deny') and that is the OPPOSITE tuning from the disguised-write detector in gate-tool.ts, which is deliberately PERMISSIVE ('when in doubt, allow'). Not an inconsistency — the cost of a false positive is asymmetric in opposite directions: there it blocks the USER from running their own tests, here it only blocks the AGENT, which retries with a thinner file and loses a turn. Do not 'harmonize' them.

shape_check._markup_comment: Judged by the line cap only. An HTML or JSON skeleton is legitimately all 'content' — it has no bodies to leave empty, so a statement budget would deny every honest scaffold.
shape_check._vocabulary: Failing closed is safe but only USABLE if the recognizer speaks the language in front of it. Measuring that (tests/fixtures/shape-languages.ts) showed the original regexes spoke FOUR languages -- TS/JS, Python, C#, Java -- while this list has twenty. Nine of thirteen honest skeletons were denied, and since the allowance is 0 at levels 3-5 a single false positive kills the whole file, so eleven extensions were effectively unusable. Fixed post-v0.5.1 by giving the recognizer vocabulary, NOT by softening the polarity. Two rules keep that honest: loose rules are GATED BY EXTENSION so SQL's column rule cannot judge TypeScript, and every loose rule is guarded by a statement-keyword denylist. Scenario S36 measures both directions and will not pass a checker that simply denies everything.
shape_check._sql_note: .sql is handled by language-gated rules: DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP of a schema object), column definitions, procedure parameters and session pragmas are structure. SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/EXEC stay statements, so the body of a stored procedure is still the user's to write -- which is the point, since this user works with SPs.
shape_check._marker_comment: The allowlist of lines that may legitimately stand in for a body. Kept short and explicit on purpose: every entry here is a hole in Layer 1, so it must be cheap to audit by reading it.

_levels_comment: authorship: what the agent may put into a file it creates. may_edit_existing is the objective create-vs-edit line — the only boundary the gate can draw without adjudicating, and the reason the whole design holds. rung_min/rung_max bound the hint ladder INSIDE the level: the level is your stable band (changes by calibration, over days), the rung is the reaction inside one problem (moves after two failures, over minutes). Collapsing them would make getting stuck on a bug demote you.

1.label: Implementer
1.summary: The agent implements; you read and get questioned.

2.label: Framer
2.summary: The agent frames structure and trivial bodies; you write the load-bearing logic.

3.label: Architect
3.summary: The agent writes skeletons and signatures; every body is yours.

4.label: Guide
4.summary: The agent writes nothing; it breaks the problem down and points at prior art in your repo.

5.label: Socratic
5.summary: The agent writes nothing and directs nothing. It asks.

6.label: Autopilot
6.summary: The axis is off. Plain code assistant, no pedagogy.
6._off_ramp: Reachable only by typing `level 6`. Calibration CLAMPS AT 5 and can never promote here by any path — an anti-atrophy plugin that promotes you to 'I do everything' sabotages itself. Kept out of argument-hint, README and QUICKSTART to discourage discovery; ALWAYS reported honestly by `status`, because discouraging discovery is not the same as hiding state from someone who already turned it on.
6._migration_role: Also the safe destination for old-v0.4 level-5 profiles: old L5 meant 'write it for me and be quiet', which under the new axis would silently mean the OPPOSITE. Both readings are 'silent', so the user would not notice until it hurt. Migrating old-L5 -> L6 preserves the exact behavior they had.
